# HELP zfs_command_stuck Whether a ZFS program that ran past its time limit has still not ended when killed (1) or not (0): ZFS itself is likely stuck on a pool, and nothing more is asked until it ends.
# TYPE zfs_command_stuck gauge
zfs_command_stuck{command="zpool"} 0
zfs_command_stuck{command="zpool_influxdb"} 0

zfs_command_timeouts_total{command="zpool_influxdb"} 1

# HELP zfs_disk_info Always 1, with what each disk in a pool is and where: ZFS's GUID for it and the path it has for it, the disk's model and world wide name, and the enclosure and slot it sits in as sas-exporter names them. The disk label is the kernel's name for the disk today, or ZFS's GUID for a disk it cannot find; the serial label is the one thing that never changes.

# HELP zfs_disk_latency_seconds How long each request to the disk took, as a histogram, since the pool was imported: compare a disk with the others in its vdev, since a stripe waits for its slowest disk. Only the time at the disk itself, wait disk, unless every disk timing is asked for. By wait: total from being asked to being answered, disk at the disk itself, and sync_queue, async_queue, scrub_queue, trim_queue and rebuild_queue in each of ZFS's queues before being sent to a disk; and by op, read or write. ZFS counts in powers of two, so each bucket ends at the most it holds, 2047ns for the one from 1024ns. ZFS keeps no total, so the sum is worked out the way zpool iostat -l works out its averages: each request counted at the middle of its bucket.

# HELP zfs_pool_request_size_bytes How big each request to the pool was, as a histogram, since the pool was imported. By queue, sync, async, scrub, trim or rebuild; op, read or write; and aggregated, true for requests ZFS made by joining smaller ones next to each other. ZFS counts in powers of two, so each bucket ends at the most it holds, 8191 bytes for the one from 4096. ZFS keeps no total, so the sum counts each request at the bottom of its bucket, since nearly every request is a power of two in size: zfs_*_bytes_total over zfs_*_operations_total is the exact average.

# HELP zfs_pool_state The pool's health, as zpool status gives it. Each state is a reading of its own, 1 for the one it is in and 0 for the rest: ONLINE, DEGRADED, FAULTED, OFFLINE, REMOVED, UNAVAIL, or SUSPENDED for a pool that has stopped reading and writing until its disks come back.
# TYPE zfs_pool_state gauge
zfs_pool_state{pool="tank",state="DEGRADED"} 1

zfs_pool_state{pool="tank",state="SUSPENDED"} 0
zfs_pool_state{pool="tank",state="UNAVAIL"} 0

# HELP zfs_up Whether the last round of asking ZFS about the pools was answered in full (1) or not (0). A pool that has stopped answering, or a program that cannot be run, shows here first.
# TYPE zfs_up gauge
zfs_up 1

# HELP zfs_vdev_fragmentation_ratio How broken up the top-level vdev's free space is, from 0 to 1, as zpool list -v shows FRAG: a vdev whose free space is in small pieces writes more slowly. The pool's FRAG is its vdevs' weighed by their size.
# TYPE zfs_vdev_fragmentation_ratio gauge

# HELP zfs_vdev_latency_seconds How long each request to the top-level vdev took, as a histogram, since the pool was imported. By wait: total from being asked to being answered, disk at the disk itself, and sync_queue, async_queue, scrub_queue, trim_queue and rebuild_queue in each of ZFS's queues before being sent to a disk; and by op, read or write. ZFS counts in powers of two, so each bucket ends at the most it holds, 2047ns for the one from 1024ns. ZFS keeps no total, so the sum is worked out the way zpool iostat -l works out its averages: each request counted at the middle of its bucket.
# TYPE zfs_vdev_latency_seconds histogram
zfs_vdev_latency_seconds_bucket{class="data",op="read",pool="tank",vdev="raidz2-0",wait="disk",le="2.047e-06"} 12
zfs_vdev_latency_seconds_bucket{class="data",op="read",pool="tank",vdev="raidz2-0",wait="disk",le="4.095e-06"} 26
zfs_vdev_latency_seconds_bucket{class="data",op="read",pool="tank",vdev="raidz2-0",wait="disk",le="+Inf"} 30
zfs_vdev_latency_seconds_sum{class="data",op="read",pool="tank",vdev="raidz2-0",wait="disk"} 9e-08
zfs_vdev_latency_seconds_count{class="data",op="read",pool="tank",vdev="raidz2-0",wait="disk"} 30
zfs_vdev_latency_seconds_bucket{class="data",op="read",pool="tank",vdev="raidz2-0",wait="total",le="2.047e-06"} 10
zfs_vdev_latency_seconds_bucket{class="data",op="read",pool="tank",vdev="raidz2-0",wait="total",le="4.095e-06"} 25
zfs_vdev_latency_seconds_bucket{class="data",op="read",pool="tank",vdev="raidz2-0",wait="total",le="+Inf"} 30
zfs_vdev_latency_seconds_sum{class="data",op="read",pool="tank",vdev="raidz2-0",wait="total"} 9e-08
zfs_vdev_latency_seconds_count{class="data",op="read",pool="tank",vdev="raidz2-0",wait="total"} 30
zfs_vdev_latency_seconds_bucket{class="data",op="write",pool="tank",vdev="raidz2-0",wait="disk",le="2.047e-06"} 1
